expectations.evidence: Consistently descriptive naming throughout: max_requests, window_seconds, _timestamps, wait_time, deficit. No abbreviated or contextual names. _evict_expired is the only slightly terse name.

Comments explain WHAT not WHY: '# Sleep briefly before retrying', 'Number of requests available in the current window'. Full Args/Returns docstrings on abstract methods. No TODOs, no references to real events.
All classes follow identical template: __init__ with validation, main method with same timeout/deadline pattern, reset() method, property. Very uniform structure.
Identical input validation pattern in both concrete classes (raise ValueError for <=0). Same try/acquire/timeout pattern everywhere. Perfectly uniform.
No signs of code evolution. Everything is perfectly clean, consistent, and intentional. No TODOs, no leftover constants, no style drift, no defensive checks from past bugs.
Formulaic docstrings with Args/Returns on abstract method. Example blocks in class docstrings for simple classes. Full descriptive docstrings on every class and public method.
